newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine grain market seen quiet over Christmas.
newsitem.headline: Philippine grain market seen quiet over Christmas.

text.p: The Philippine grains market is expected to be generally quiet in the coming week due to ample supply and the Christmas holiday period which should keep buyers sidelined, traders said on Friday.

"For wheat, I don't expect any more importation for January 1997 shipment. The next action for early 1997 will be on corn, and rice in the second half of the year," said a trader in a U.S. commodity house.
Three Philippine firms bought a total of 28,750 tonnes of U.S. dark northern spring wheat and 6,250 tonnes of western white wheat on Wednesday night.
"I expect the wheat orders for January shipments to stop next week," said another trader.
Major Philippine flour mills said they were fully stocked with wheat for their January requirements.
Philippine firms are expected to shift back to the U.S. market and other alternative grain suppliers such as Canada and Australia following storm damage to Argentina's wheat crop.
The mills said the prospect of bumper harvests in other wheat exporting countries should compensate for the crop damage in Argentina.
The Department of Trade and Industry said the prevailing local price for hard flour remained steady at 290 pesos per 25-kilo bag and 260 pesos for soft flour.
The Philippines plans to import up to 500,000 tonnes of corn in 1997, of which 300,000 tonnes are expected to be bought in the first quarter.

The National Food Authority (NFA) said some 110,000 tonnes of imported U.S. yellow corn had arrived in the country in the past few weeks. "We expected two more ships carrying 27,500 tonnes each on December 26," an official said.
The average retail price of local white corn rose to 11.88 pesos per kg from 11.41 pesos last week, while yellow corn slid to 10.72 pesos per kg from 11.13, the NFA said.
The average farm-gate price of white corn dropped to 6.06 pesos from 6.40 and yellow corn dropped to 6.53 pesos per kg from 6.40.
The NFA said the Phillipine rice stock was 1.37 million tonnes on December, while corn inventories stood at 425,000 tonnes.
The NFA also said it had 1.9 million tonnes of unmilled rice in its warehouses nationwide. "This is equal to 1.235 million tonnes of (milled) rice," an NFA official said.
The country requires 20,500 tonnes of rice and 14,600 tonnes of corn daily.
The Philippines also plans to import between 300,000 to 500,000 tonnes of rice in the second quarter of 1997.
On Thursday, Pracha Charutrakulchai, head of the Foreign Trade Department in the Thai Commerce Ministry said the Philippines had expressed interest in buying rice from Thailand and Vietnam.
"All the discussions were preliminary. Any orders that will be made next year depend on the rice output in the first semester of 1997," an NFA official said in response.
